title: ServiceManifest
description: PLACEHOLDER. The platform team's real service-manifest schema replaces this file; keep the filename so `checks.manifest_valid` and the tests keep working. This minimal version exists so the factory can validate that a work item declared what the platform needs (name, runtime, health endpoint, env vars with a secret flag, migrations command, resources). Every field here is expected to survive in the real schema; the real schema will add more. The manifest lives at a fixed path in the application repository named by the platform-contract skill.

test_environment.description: Factory-managed isolated test setup. Used identically for onboarding an existing app and generating a greenfield scaffold.

profile.description: Repository-relative path to a test_environment.schema.json profile. No credentials.

service.description: Service name as the platform knows it; becomes part of the preview URL.

kind.description: Runtime family the platform supports (for example container, cloud-run, function). Enum left open on purpose; the real schema closes it.

entrypoint.description: Command the platform runs to start the service.

setup.description: Optional command that installs what the test plan and the entrypoint need, run once per verification from the repository root inside a fresh per-run virtual environment (its bin directory first on PATH, VIRTUAL_ENV set). Without it the orchestrator installs the repository's pyproject (`-e .[dev]`, or the declared dependency lists when the project is not installable). A setup that exits non-zero is a failed deterministic check.

path.description: HTTP path the platform probes for readiness.

env.description: Every environment variable the service reads. Secrets are delivered by the platform; the manifest only declares them.

command.description: Run by the platform before the new revision receives traffic.

additive_only.description: Declares that migrations in this revision never drop or rewrite existing data.
